- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above recent high.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +0.5–1.0% bias to first 5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift direction.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
- In high-sentiment periods (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.67+), model tends to overreact; apply downward correction of 1–2% after 3 consecutive bullish sentiment days.
- If true price exceeds model forecast by >3% for 2+ consecutive days, model is underestimating trend; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
